turns.text: My roommate has epilepsy and had a seizure last night, and I felt completely helpless. What should I do during and after a seizure?
Why do they say not to hold someone down or put anything in their mouth? I'd like to understand the reasons.
How do I protect his head, and when should I move him onto his side?
If I asked an epilepsy nurse, what would she want me to learn first?
What do first-aid instructors teach about timing a seizure and why it matters?
A friend says her brother's seizures are followed by hours of confusion. Is that normal, and how do I handle it?
Someone else told me to note what happened just before, and film it if I can. Is that actually useful?
We're students with no one else around and it will happen again. What should we set up in the flat?
Exactly when do I call an ambulance?
Could you give me a step-by-step plan — during, after, what to time and note, when to call for help — I can stick on the fridge?
